name: Primary Cutaneous Amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Cutaneous Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Presence of persistent pruritic, hyperpigmented or hypopigmented macules or papules localized to the skin without systemic involvement
Demonstration of amyloid deposits in the papillary dermis by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Absence of systemic amyloidosis confirmed by clinical evaluation and laboratory testing
Characteristic dermoscopic features such as central hub and radiating streaks

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, histopathology confirmation, and exclusion of systemic amyloidosis) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on skin biopsy and exclusion of systemic involvement

pathognomonic.notes: Typically on the upper back, arms, and legs
searchTerms: itchy darkened skin spots or bumps
itchy skin patches with increased pigment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposits in papillary dermis confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: protein deposits in skin confirmed by biopsy
amyloid buildup in upper skin layer
abnormal protein accumulation in skin tissue
skin lichenification due to chronic irritation

common.symptomName: Dermoscopy showing central hub and radiating streaks
searchTerms: skin exam showing central spot with radiating lines
dermoscopy revealing hub and streak pattern
characteristic skin lesion pattern on microscopy

occasional.notes: May be present due to irritation

searchTerms: thinning or wasting of skin in one area

laboratory: Negative systemic amyloidosis markers (normal serum and urine protein electrophoresis)
Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
imaging: Not typically required; imaging used to exclude systemic amyloidosis if suspected
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; familial cases reported rarely
other: Skin biopsy with Congo red staining showing amyloid deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of amyloid deposits on biopsy
More pronounced lichenification without amyloid staining
Presence of systemic symptoms (e.g., renal, cardiac involvement)
Similar amyloid deposits but different clinical presentation

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss, fatigue, or organ dysfunction
Presence of nodular or tumefactive lesions suggestive of systemic amyloidosis
references: Wang, X., et al. Primary Cutaneous Amyloidosis: Clinical Features and Diagnosis. Journal of Dermatology, 2022.
Orphanet Report on Primary Cutaneous Amyloidosis, ORPHA:137807.
James, W.D., et al. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 14th Edition, 2020.
